reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.energy -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: the H^2 "energy" of an integrand,
  E int_0^T |Z_t|^2 dt   (sec. 3: H^2_W norm E int_0^T |Z_t|_F^2 dt; the Ito isometry
  E|int_0^T Z dW|^2 = E int_0^T |Z|^2 dt, used in Lemma bpbsde and throughout sec. 4),
i.e. the squared L^2(dt x dP) norm of the integrand on [0,T] (or on [0,t] for the integral up to
t). Faithful Lean: the integral over Omega of the time integral over [0,T] (or the stated
interval) of |Z(t,omega)|^2 w.r.t. Lebesgue x P, either as a lintegral in [0,oo] (then the
value oo for non-square-integrable Z is the correct value, not junk) or as a real Bochner
integral (then 0 is the junk value for non-integrable Z, harmless only when every use also
assumes the integrability). Time interval should be [0,T] (Ioc/Icc equal a.e.). The order of
integration is immaterial (Tonelli) for a jointly measurable Z. Not faithful: a sum over a
partition that is not the integral, the wrong exponent, or integrating over [0,oo) when the
claim is on [0,T].

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.energy (ItoIntegrandComplete.lean:30-32)

Reading: E int_0^T |Z_t|^2 dt, the squared L^2(dt x dP) norm on [0,T]; lintegral in [0,oo] (value
oo meaningful) or Bochner; interval [0,T] up to null sets; order immaterial (Tonelli).
Lean: energy P T H = int^- omega, int^- s in Icc 0 T, (||H omega s||_+)^2 d(volume) dP, an
ENNReal lower Lebesgue integral. ||.||_+ on R is |.|, squared; time window Icc 0 T; P outer,
Lebesgue inner. energy_eq_eLpNorm_sq identifies it with the squared L^2 seminorm on
(Omega x R, P x Leb|[0,T]) for jointly measurable H. Value oo for non-square-integrable H is the
correct value (not junk): consumers use "energy ... != top" for H^2 membership and "= 0" for
equality in H^2 (WP uniqueness clause), both correct readings. For a non-measurable H the
lintegral is a lower integral, but every consumer in the propositions has H predictable or
jointly measurable. Matrix integrands: consumers sum energy over coordinates (k,j), giving
E int |Z|_F^2. Matches the reading.
Verdict: faithful.

author_review.disagreements:
No disagreement on substance. The reviewer labels it "faithful with representation choices"
(iterated ENNReal lower integral; real-valued integrands with the Frobenius norm assembled as a
sum over entries); I labelled it "faithful", treating those as the definition of the notion
rather than choices. Both readings agree that the value is E int_0^T |H|^2 dt for measurable H
and that the ENNReal value top is meaningful, not junk. I accept the reviewer's label as the more
explicit one.
